title: Monolithic Prelude Modules
pattern: Creating a single, massive `prelude` module that re-exports almost every utility, trait, helper, and struct in the entire codebase, and importing it wholesale (`use crate::prelude::*;`) in every file.
why_bad: Massive compile-time overhead and complete loss of dependency clarity. Developers can no longer identify where a specific type or trait is imported from, turning the codebase into a spaghettified dependency mess where any file can access any internal detail.
detection: Look for a `prelude.rs` module that exports more than 30 distinct types from disjoint modules, combined with wildcards (`*`) importing that prelude across almost every source file.
counterexample: Cohesive library preludes that export a small, tightly curated set of vital traits (like the standard library prelude or a serialization library's core traits).
fix: Use targeted imports. Export only highly omnipresent, fundamental traits in preludes, and force explicit module paths or imports for concrete types.
source: *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 6; *Titus Winters et al. - Software Engineering at Google (2020)*, Chapter 15, "Dependency Management".
